title: Seoul cafés, BBQ & fried chicken: 15 places to eat
desc: Seoul food spots grouped into cafés and bakeries, market food, fried chicken, Korean BBQ, Korean-fusion and bars.

items.title: Soha Salt Pond (소하염전)
items.memo: Salt bread in flavors like truffle and peanut.

items.title: Jayeondo Sogeumppang (자연도소금빵)
items.memo: Sells salt bread in packs of four; quick kiosk ordering.

items.title: Alto Coffee Bar (알토)
items.memo: Small espresso bar known for excellent espresso.

items.title: Cafe Onion Anguk (카페어니언 안국)
items.memo: Pastries in a 1920s hanok; rich and messy, so eat in.

items.title: Cheese Industry (치즈인더스트리)
items.memo: Ranch-themed bakery with cheese desserts and cheese drinks.

items.title: Gwangjang Market (광장시장)
items.memo: Classic market: bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, tteokbokki. Food tours available.

items.title: Hyodo Chicken (효도치킨)
items.memo: Fried chicken with anchovy and shishito flavors.

items.title: Kyochon Pilbang (교촌필방)
items.memo: Speakeasy-style chicken spot with a multi-course omakase option.

items.title: Kukbingwan (국빈관)
items.memo: 100% Korean beef over charcoal; staff help first-timers grill.

items.title: Wangbijib Myeongdong (왕비집 명동)
items.memo: Samgyeopsal, bulgogi and lots of banchan in Myeongdong.

items.title: Woo Mool Zip (우물집)
items.memo: Private rooms and set menus in a traditional-style setting.

items.title: Jangin Dakgalbi Hongdae (장인닭갈비 홍대)
items.memo: Spicy dakgalbi with optional cheese; big portions.

items.title: Ikseon Chwihyang (익선취향)
items.memo: Korean-Italian fusion; cream and rosé pastas.

items.title: Seongsu Darak (성수다락)
items.memo: Spicy ragu pasta and a creamy omelette.

items.title: Art Monster Ikseon-dong (아트몬스터 익선동)
items.memo: Craft beer bar with plants and neon; truffle pizza on the menu.
